clue.text: Extent of Terry's unusual woodwork

indicators.note: something unusual is out of the ordinary, so the letters before it leave their ordinary order

parts.note: the two words taken letter for letter, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Someone marvels at how far Terry's odd carpentry projects have gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extent' does no work in the wordplay; FORESTRY can also mean a tract of wooded land, which may be what the setter had in mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Forestry is the tending and harvesting of trees, playfully called work done in the woods.

clue.text: Going after birds (incurs a penalty we hear)

indicators.note: what we hear is a spoken sound, so the word is identified by how it is pronounced

parts.note: committing a foul in sport earns a penalty

explanation.surface: A sportsman's bird-chasing habit keeps getting him penalised.
explanation.definitionFit: Fowling is the sport of hunting wild birds such as ducks and pheasants.

clue.text: Did Newton get wet noting their message?

definitions.text: Did Newton get wet noting their message?

parts.note: surface reading: the scientist caught in a shower
setter's reading: falling water, like his apple, carries the message that things fall, read as two words

explanation.surface: Was Isaac Newton soaked while studying what the falling water told him?
explanation.walkthrough: Newton is famed for noting that an apple drops; split the answer into RAIN DROPS and the message of the falling water is the same law.
explanation.definitionFit: Raindrops are the individual drops of water falling from clouds as rain.

clue.text: Designer's plate embarrasses clients

indicators.note: to embarrass is to throw someone into confusion, so the following letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A designer's work plate causes awkwardness for the customers.
explanation.definitionFit: A stencil is a cut-out plate through which a designer brushes paint to reproduce a pattern.

clue.text: Engineer sent urgent message ' to have the system connected again

definitions.note: a phrase for the verb; the answer is its past tense

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, the British army's engineering corps
to wire is to send a telegram

explanation.surface: An engineer telegraphs urgently asking for the system to be reconnected.
explanation.walkthrough: RE for an engineer is a standard crossword abbreviation; wiring a message is old slang for telegraphing.
explanation.definitionFit: Rewired means fitted with new electrical wiring, giving a building's circuits fresh connections.

clue.text: Is this Burgundy as dry as it sounds?

indicators.note: how something sounds is its pronunciation, so the wine's name is judged by ear

parts.note: bone-dry means completely dry

explanation.surface: A wine buff wonders whether this red Burgundy really is as dry as its name suggests.
explanation.walkthrough: The wine's French name is pronounced like the English bone, as in bone-dry.
explanation.definitionFit: Beaune is a town in Burgundy whose wines are sold under its name, so it stands for a Burgundy.

clue.text: Polish drug for animals

parts.note: to buff is to polish
aloes is a bitter purgative drug

explanation.surface: A Polish medicine intended for use on livestock.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital P makes it look like the nationality; it is the verb meaning to shine.
explanation.definitionFit: Buffaloes are large wild or domesticated oxen, so they are animals.

clue.text: Like the young men of the fifties, only .more so

definitions.text: Like the young men of the fifties, only .more so

parts.words: Like the young men of the fifties
parts.note: surface reading: resembling youths of that decade
setter's reading: the comparative of the adjective attached to the Angry Young Men

explanation.surface: Describing someone who outdoes the young men of the 1950s.
explanation.walkthrough: The Angry Young Men were a group of 1950s British writers such as John Osborne; more so than angry is the comparative.
explanation.definitionFit: Angrier is the comparative of angry, so it means more furious than the famous writers were.

clue.text: So-called wild Lion-man .

indicators.note: something wild is untamed and disorderly, so the letters after it run riot

parts.note: the hyphenated word taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A savage creature that is half lion, half man, at least by name.
explanation.definitionFit: Nominal means existing in name only, just as a so-called thing is merely called that.

clue.text: Diminutive blond star, . dense and not very bright

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a small fair-haired person, read as two words

definitions.text: star, . dense and not very bright
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a small compact faint star

explanation.surface: A short blonde celebrity who is thick and dim-witted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dense and not very bright' sounds like an insult to the actress but is astronomy: such stars are extremely compact and faint.
explanation.definitionFit: A white dwarf is the small, very dense, dim remnant of a burnt-out star.

clue.text: Spirited flock of swans

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the old collective noun for a group of these birds

explanation.surface: A lively group of swans.
explanation.definitionFit: Game means brave and ready for anything, and a game of swans is a traditional collective term.

clue.text: Takeover bid to a mind?

parts.note: surface reading: a company's offer to buy another
setter's reading: an attempt to take over someone's thinking

explanation.surface: A corporate buyout offer, aimed oddly at a person's mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Indoctrination is teaching someone to accept beliefs uncritically, seizing control of how they think.

clue.text: Complained that the seventh row went in front

parts.note: G is the seventh letter of the alphabet
taken as written
led means went ahead

explanation.surface: Someone grumbled that row seven had pushed in ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: To growl is to grumble in a low surly voice, so growled means voiced a complaint.

clue.text: Do oddfellows move in such circles?

definitions.text: Do oddfellows move in such circles?

parts.words: Do oddfellows move in such circles
parts.note: surface reading: the social set of the friendly society
setter's reading: odd fellows are peculiar people, and circles not sharing a centre suit them

explanation.surface: Asking about the social world of the Oddfellows friendly society.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oddfellows are a British friendly society; peculiar people and off-centre circles share the same adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Eccentric describes both an odd person and circles that do not share a common centre.

clue.text: How many evangelists go to and fro with this sort of yarn?

parts.note: Matthew, Mark, Luke and John wrote the Gospels
to ply is to travel back and forth regularly

explanation.surface: A puzzle about the Gospel writers travelling with a tall tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yarn' suggests a story, but it is knitting wool.
explanation.definitionFit: Four-ply describes knitting wool made of four twisted strands, a common thickness of yarn.

clue.text: Wandering bird-man?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a falcon, and also a man's first name

explanation.surface: A roving birdwatcher.
explanation.definitionFit: Peregrine means foreign or migratory, names a fast falcon, and is a man's given name too.

clue.text: Lorenzo's fair torchbearer

parts.note: surface reading: a lovely girl carrying a light for her lover
setter's reading: in The Merchant of Venice Shylock's daughter elopes disguised as a page carrying a torch

explanation.surface: The beautiful woman who carries a torch for Lorenzo.
explanation.walkthrough: To carry a torch is also to be in love, which she is with Lorenzo in Shakespeare's play.
explanation.definitionFit: Shylock's daughter in The Merchant of Venice runs off with Lorenzo dressed as his torch-carrying page.

clue.text: Farthest MS noted for revision

indicators.note: a revision rewrites and rearranges a text, so the letters given are reordered

parts.note: MS is a manuscript, taken here as its two letters

explanation.surface: The most remote manuscript has been marked for an author's corrections.
explanation.definitionFit: Endmost means situated at the very end, the furthest away of all.

clue.text: Sent round faulty gem — portion cut off

indicators.note: something faulty is defective, so its letters are out of order
going round something encloses it, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: taken as written
the word's letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A flawed jewel was sent back, with a piece chipped off.
explanation.definitionFit: A segment is a section or part divided off from a whole.

clue.text: Hopes to get snakes to contain their anger

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: asps are venomous snakes
ire is wrath

explanation.surface: Someone wants to make vipers keep their rage in check.
explanation.definitionFit: To aspire is to hope or long for something, so aspires means hopes.

clue.text: "The Brothers" of Terence's theatre

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the Roman playwright's comedy, titled with the Greek word for brothers
second meaning: a well-known playhouse on the Strand in London

explanation.surface: A Roman comedy staged at the dramatist's own playhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: Terence's comedy Adelphi takes its name from Greek for brothers, and London has an Adelphi Theatre.

clue.text: Plain sort of oysters to pick up?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a broad grassy flatland

definitions.text: sort of oysters to pick up?
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the raw-egg hangover cure, a pick-me-up

explanation.surface: Asking about an ordinary kind of shellfish to gather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pick up' suggests collecting oysters, but a prairie oyster, a raw egg with seasoning, is a pick-me-up for a hangover.
explanation.definitionFit: A prairie is a vast flat grassland, and prairie oysters are a well-known restorative drink.

clue.text: Performer well up on theatre work

definitions.text: Performer well up on theatre work

parts.note: to surge is to rise up like a wave
taken as written

explanation.surface: An actor who knows all about stagecraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Theatre' points to the stage, but the theatre here is the operating theatre, where this performer operates.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgeon performs operations and is expert in work done in the operating theatre.

clue.text: Does a form of hoarding get men beastly selfish?

indicators.note: a form of something is a new shape of it, so the letters are moulded into another order

parts.note: the three words taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Does stockpiling make men horribly self-centred?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beastly' belongs to the definition: the idiom features an animal, the dog in Aesop's fable that keeps the ox from hay it cannot eat itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog-in-the-manger attitude spitefully withholds from others something one has no use for oneself.

clue.text: Mud from the said river?

indicators.note: what is said is spoken aloud, so the river's name is taken by its pronunciation

parts.note: the Ouse is a river in Yorkshire and also one in Sussex

explanation.surface: Sludge dredged up from a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ouse is the name of several English rivers.
explanation.definitionFit: Ooze is soft wet mud, especially the slime on a river or sea bed.

clue.text: Put in another estimate and get approval

parts.note: to reap is to gain or obtain
praise is approving words

explanation.surface: A contractor resubmits a quote and wins approval for it.
explanation.definitionFit: To reappraise is to assess the value of something afresh, giving a new valuation.

clue.text: The way a spasm can cause interference

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
taken as written
a tic is an involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: How a muscle twitch might disrupt things.
explanation.definitionFit: Static is crackling noise on a radio caused by electrical disturbance in the signal.

clue.text: Voluble number

parts.note: surface reading: talkative
setter's reading: the figure from the phrase for talking incessantly, to the dozen

explanation.walkthrough: A voluble person talks nineteen to the dozen, a British idiom for chattering very fast.
explanation.definitionFit: The figure one more than eighteen is the one in the idiom about rapid nonstop talking.
